newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIA-TV TUBES MAKER EKRANAS SEE STRONG PROFIT '96.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIA-TV TUBES MAKER EKRANAS SEE STRONG PROFIT '96.

text.p: Lithuania's television tubes producer Ekranas reported an unaudited net profit of 1996 rose to 45.6 million litas from a loss of 13.8 million litas a year ago on Tuesday.
Company spokeswoman Angelija Zokaitiene said the company operated profitably last year but the steep gain was also explained by the government writing of around 39 million litas of overdue payments.
These debts were accumulated in 1992-1993 during a period of hyper-inflation period.
The government also wrote-off another 14.2 million litas in exchange of for Ekranas giving the state a building it owned in Panevezhys in north Lithuania.
Ekranas said in the statement that its turnover in 1996 was 331.1 million litas versus 291.7 million a year ago.
The company also reported its gross profit last year was 69.5 million litas and its operating profit was 12.9 million litas.
The company said its assets in 1996 were 250.6 million litas.
"The results of Coopers and Lybrand audit are expected before the end of this week," Zokaitiene told Reuters.

"The company has its development strategy and the main shareholders will suggest to the shareholder's meeting on March 26 to keep the major stake of 1996 and 1997 profit within the institution to invest it in the production line development."
Ekranas share capital is 113 million litas and 44 percent of its shares are held by Swiss Farimex.
The rest of shares are held privately including by employees and managment of the company.
Zokaitiene said 92.6 percent of its products the company exports to around 20 countries, including Turkey, Italy, Germany and Great Britain mainly.
Ekranas is listed on the group A on the country's stock exchange and was quoted at 7.0 litas on Monday.
